description: Known-answer vectors for end-to-end encrypted team members' email addresses, v1 (Pulse/docs/plans/07-11-2026-team-names-e2e-design.md §16.2), the email kind of the team-names construction: the same identity keys and envelope, HPKE (RFC 9180) mode_auth with DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM, aad = 0x01, plaintext = I2OSP(len, 2) || utf8(email) || zeros to 512 bytes, sealed = 0x01 || enc || ct (594 bytes); info = info_label || 0x00 || team_id || sender_id || recipient_id (UUIDs as 16 raw bytes, 69 bytes in all); sealed_hash = SHA-256(sealed); email_tag = HMAC-SHA256(tag_secret, tag_label || 0x00 || utf8(email) || team_id || recipient_key_id || sealed_hash)[0:16]; key_id = SHA-256(public_key). An address is sealed and shown only if it is valid UTF-8 of at most max_email_bytes bytes with exactly one '@' (U+0040), at least one character on each side of it, and no whitespace (White_Space), separator (Z), control (Cc) or format (Cf) character; nothing folds case, normalises or trims. names_info_label is the team-names kind's, for cross_kind_negatives. Ephemeral keys, DEKs and nonces are fixed here and random in production; none repeats team-names-v1.json's. Generated by the standard-library Go reference that made team-names-v1.json, which reproduces RFC 9180 A.3.1, A.3.3, A.6.1 and A.6.3; every seal in this file equals Cloudflare CIRCL's output for the same inputs. All hex.

seals.description: the same address to another recipient
the shortest address: one character on each side of the '@'
three-byte UTF-8 on both sides of the '@' (an internationalised address, RFC 6531)
upper case, sealed and opened as it is (nothing folds case)
the pair and address of seal 0 in the other team
254 bytes, the longest address that may be sealed
254 bytes of UTF-8 in 132 UTF-16 code units
four-byte UTF-8 (a surrogate pair in JavaScript)
every RFC 5322 atext symbol as the local part

open_negatives.description: sender and recipient ids swapped in info
another recipient id in info (F's id, E's key)
opened with another recipient's key (F for E's row)
opened against another sender's key (F's for D's row)
sealed with aad 0x02 under wire version 0x01
a body truncated by one byte
a body one byte too long
a non-zero padding byte after a valid address
invalid UTF-8 (a surrogate code point encoded as ED A0 80)

address_negatives.description: a fullwidth commercial at (U+FF20) in place of the '@'
255 bytes of UTF-8 in 133 UTF-16 code units

cross_kind_negatives.description: an email row (seal 0) opened as a name, with the team-names info
a team-names row of the same address opened as an email, with the team-emails info

tag_negatives.description: the tag over another row's sealed bytes
the tag for another recipient key
the tag of the address in another case (nothing folds case)
the tag under another person's tag secret
row 0's metadata over another ciphertext (its enc kept, the 528 bytes after it replaced)

envelope_negatives.description: D's envelope under the vault's own context
